Standardising two-year rental subsidy release; owners who haven't signed acquisition letters also benefit

The government announced today that regardless of which option owners choose after selling their property titles—including receiving cash only, receiving cash and then joining the "Special Sales Scheme", the "flat-for-flat" scheme, or ultimately failing to select a suitable unit under the "Special Sales Scheme"—all will be eligible to receive a two-year rental subsidy until 21 December 2027. The arrangement also applies to owners who have yet to sign the "Letter of Acceptance of Acquisition Offer".

As for owners who participate in the "Special Sales Scheme", if the occupancy date of the unit is after 21 December 2027, the foundation will continue to disburse the rental subsidy. The government indicated that, considering owners generally need three months to renovate their new homes, owners' eligibility for the rental subsidy will be maintained until three months from the date of the assignment of the new unit purchased, after which the next instalment of the rental subsidy will cease.

Cheuk Wing-hing: Optimising arrangements with a "people-first" approach after hearing concerns

Deputy Chief Secretary Cheuk Wing-hing stated on a radio programme that residents and legislators had expressed concerns about the original arrangements, including being unable to identify a unit immediately after selling their property titles, being unable to select a suitable unit after joining the scheme, and being unable to terminate current tenancy agreements. After listening to the views and giving them due consideration, the authorities decided to adopt a "people-first" approach and optimise the rental arrangements to provide greater flexibility for residents.

Government previously stated on Monday that owners who failed to select flats would only receive rental subsidy until the acquisition payment was credited

In December 2025, the government announced it would provide Wang Fuk Court owners with an annual rental subsidy of $150,000, disbursed half-yearly at $75,000 per instalment. However, after the long-term housing arrangement plan was announced in February, some members of the explanation team told residents that they would need to vacate transitional housing within 30 days of accepting the acquisition, and that the subsidy would cease immediately upon receipt of payment, giving rise to concerns.

On 13 March, the government issued a statement to "clarify inaccurate reports", stating that the 30-day vacancy requirement was not a hard-and-fast rule, and that if owners sold their property titles and received cash without joining the "Special Sales Scheme", the rental subsidy would be disbursed until the relevant funds were credited; if they joined the scheme, the subsidy would be disbursed until the occupancy date of the relevant subsidised housing unit.

Media reports emerged recently indicating that some residents were told by the explanation team that even if they participated in the "Special Sales Scheme", failing to complete flat selection by September would be treated as non-participation, and the rental subsidy would cease. The government stated on Monday (the 13th) that if owners were unable to purchase a unit under the "Special Sales Scheme", the subsidy would be disbursed until the acquisition payment was credited—only to backtrack today (the 17th), stating that a standardised two-year rental subsidy would be issued.
